transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-04
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Priya Sharma (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Lina Wu (Redwood CSM); Dana Ortiz (Peregrine Head of ML), Rajesh Patel (Platform Eng), Marta Klein (Finance), Tom Hale (SRE)

Summary:
Quick operational checkpoint ahead of Peregrine's Q4 promotion window. Review last month's usage spike, reconcile cost overages vs expected burn, talk reliability mitigations, and align on a hybrid pilot (reserved Dedicated capacity for peak plus hosted fallback). Agree to share security artefacts and run an internal Redwood perf sim against customer's traces.

Shared links referenced during call:
- Hybrid pilot pricing spreadsheet (placeholder link: https://redwood.app/sheets/hybrid-pilot-pricing)
- SOC2+ISO scoping doc (https://redwood.app/docs/security/soc2-iso)
- Workload trace upload instructions (S3 presigned link sent to Rajesh)

Transcript body (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Priya Sharma: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to do a short checkpoint before your promo starts next week, make sure the runway is clear. Lina, quick intro?
[00:08] Lina Wu: Hey all, quick intros. Dana, Rajesh, Marta, Tom from Peregrine. Priya, Marco from our side.
[00:14] Dana Ortiz: Yep thanks, just to flag we had a spike during last month's staging test, costs went up, latency bumped for 95th pct, wanted to understand mitigations and whether Dedicated makes sense for peak traffic.
[00:26] Marco Diaz: Got it. We looked at the traces you shared earlier, there was a, uh, a sequence-length shift and some long-tail tokens causing extra KV cache pressure — we have a few knobs to tighten that.
[00:38] Rajesh Patel: Quick question, when you say KV cache pressure, are you referring to the distributed cache in the Redwood runtime or our app-side cache? We saw heavy mem IO on the GPU hosts.
[00:50] Marco Diaz: Good call, it's the runtime KV cache; at high concurrency the cache retention increased which meant more context reloads. We can tune cache TTL and batching thresholds; for Dedicated we can also increase per-pod memory.
[01:05] Marta Klein: From finance — can you give a ballpark of Dedicated cost vs hosted during spikes? We need to justify the reserve.
[01:13] Priya Sharma: Sure, high level: Dedicated has a higher fixed commit but lower per-token marginal cost under sustained peaks. For short bursts, hosted with burst capacity is often cheaper — but for Peregrine's 6 hour daily spike pattern, Dedicated looks attractive. We'll send a modeled burn sheet.
[01:33] Tom Hale: Also need to confirm RD's fallback behavior — if Dedicated nodes are exhausted, do requests fail or route to hosted? What's the SLA?
[01:43] Marco Diaz: You can configure smart routing: canary to hosted variant, or fail open. SLA for Dedicated is higher, we have an automatic fallback policy that will route compatible model variants to hosted with a predefined latency/cost tradeoff.
[02:00] Dana Ortiz: Are model variants downgraded automatically? Concerned about quality regression mid-promo.
[02:06] Marco Diaz: There's a policy to prefer same model family first; you can set hard fallbacks to prevent auto-downgrade. We also support canary A/B to compare outputs.
[02:18] Rajesh Patel: About security: we need VPC-only ingress, KMS integration, and audit logs for all token usage. How mature are those features?
[02:28] Priya Sharma: Private deployments support VPC and KMS/HSM integrations — our audit logs include token-level events. We'll share the SOC2/ISO docs and the HSM/KMS whitepaper. Lina will follow up.
[02:40] Marta Klein: And data residency — some data slices must stay in eu-west-1 for GDPR. Can Dedicated be region pinned?
[02:48] Marco Diaz: Yes, you can pin model pools and routing by region; for hybrid we can localize the Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 and route EU traffic there.
[02:58] Dana Ortiz: Ok, the performance ask: can Redwood run a bench with our traces? We want numbers matching our token distribution and sequence lengths.
[03:06] Priya Sharma: Yes, Marco will run an internal perf sim if you upload 3 representative traces. We'll return p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens with suggested batching/quant profiles.
[03:20] Rajesh Patel: Onboarding timeline: how fast can Dedicated be provisioned? We might need capacity within two weeks.
[03:27] Marco Diaz: For standard Dedicated pools in public regions it's 3-7 days once the commit is approved; for private on-prem it's longer. If you accept a pilot with a small reserved pool we can aim for 5 days.
[03:39] Marta Klein: Any long-term commit minimums? We try to avoid big lock-ins.
[03:44] Priya Sharma: We offer monthly and annual reserved tiers; pilots can be month-to-month with conversion discounts if you commit longer term. We'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[03:56] Tom Hale: We ran into a throttling event last week where our request pipeline was backpressured — are there guaranteed concurrency limits?
[04:04] Marco Diaz: You can set per-token quotas and per-route concurrency SLOs. Throttling will be surfaced on the console and we have autoscale burst policies. We'll also recommend a queueing front to smooth spikes.
[04:18] Dana Ortiz: A random nit — we saw the runtime log say "K V cash" in an export, eh — transcript/telemetry naming sometimes not consistent. Not a blocker.
[04:26] Priya Sharma: Ha, yeah that's the speech-to-text. :)
[04:30] [--skip ahead to mid-call details around 20m mark--]
[20:05] Marco Diaz: Results from the first pass perf sim: with sequence lengths pinned to your 95th distribution, switching to continuous batching + 4-bit quant saves ~28% per token cost with minimal latency impact in Dedicated. On hosted variants quantization introduces some variance; we can knob for quality.
[20:22] Dana Ortiz: Is 4-bit quant safe for our LLM? We have hallucination sensitivity on customer-facing flows.
[20:29] Marco Diaz: We recommend running your eval suites; Redwood Optimize can run model/regression checks tied to prompt sets. If regressions exceed thresholds we won't enable aggressive quant by default.
[20:40] Marta Klein: From a finance POV that 28% is promising provided quality holds. Can you produce a cost curve comparing 100k, 1M, 10M tokens per day?
[20:50] Priya Sharma: Yes — pricing sheet will include multiple scenarios and escalation triggers.
[21:00] Rajesh Patel: Network egress for eu region — do you charge cross-region egress if failover routes to us-east-1? We need to avoid surprise egress costs.
[21:09] Priya Sharma: We can configure routing to avoid cross-region failovers; if cross-region happens there can be egress fees — we'll show that on the model. Also you can pin routes to prevent auto-failover to other regions.
[21:24] Tom Hale: Ok, for the pilot we want: small Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 scaled to handle the expected promo peak for 6 hours, hosted fallback disabled for quality, plus SOC2 audit review.
[21:35] Priya Sharma: Sounds good. We'll prepare a pilot SOW that captures capacity, SLA, rollback and success criteria.
[21:42] Dana Ortiz: Success criteria: p95 latency below 350ms for canonical flows, errors < 0.1%, and cost within 15% of forecast.
[21:52] Marco Diaz: Noted. We'll instrument custom metrics and add tracing hooks in the console for token-level breakdown.
[22:02] Marta Klein: When will you need the PO? If pilot pricing is acceptable we can get finance approval quickly.
[22:08] Priya Sharma: If we get sign-off on the pilot by next Tuesday we can provision by the following Monday. We'll send PO templates with net-30 and options.
[22:20] Rajesh Patel: Any hidden operational work on our side for VPC peering/route tables? We prefer minimal changes.
[22:28] Marco Diaz: For Dedicated in VPC mode there is some networking setup — we'll provide IaC snippets and a checklist to minimize lift. Our SE team will partner during the window.
[22:40] Dana Ortiz: About audit: who handles key rotation when using your KMS integration? We need rotation policies to satisfy our auditors.
[22:49] Priya Sharma: You control the customer KMS keys; Redwood integrates with your KMS and respects your rotation schedule. We'll document the flow for auditors.
[22:58] Tom Hale: Are there logs for each token call that we can ship to our SIEM? We want to maintain a full chain of custody for requests.
[23:07] Marco Diaz: Audit logs include token-level metadata and can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure forwarders. We'll include sample retention policies.
[23:16] [brief cross-talk on minor calendar logistics]
[23:28] Lina Wu: I'll share the SOC2 package and the HSM/KMS whitepaper right after this call. Also I'll create a short onboarding checklist for the pilot.
[23:36] Marta Klein: Great. Also can you add a line item for chargeback attribution per product team? We need to track costs per route.
[23:44] Priya Sharma: Yes, per-route cost breakdown is a console feature — we'll ensure you'll have token-level attribution exported to your FinOps.
[23:54] Dana Ortiz: A final thought — if we see heavy variance on quality after quant, what's the rollback plan? We need immediate ability to revert to full-precision model.
[24:02] Marco Diaz: We maintain pinned model versions and instantaneous routing switches; rollback can be automated with a simple policy if regressions are detected. We'll run fail-safe tests during pilot.
[24:16] [closing 10 minutes: recap and confirm next steps]
[32:12] Priya Sharma: Recap: we'll send pricing scenarios, Marco runs perf sim once traces are uploaded, Lina sends SOC2 and KMS docs, customer to review and provide PO window.
[32:25] Dana Ortiz: Agreed. Timing: we'll try to get traces uploaded today or tomorrow.
[32:32] Marta Klein: Finance will review the pilot numbers; we'll respond by Friday.
[32:38] Priya Sharma: Perfect. Any other questions?
[32:42] Rajesh Patel: One last tech question — do you provide a test harness or local docker image for preflight?
[32:49] Marco Diaz: We have a local runner and docker image for private/on-prem customers; for hosted we provide a synthetic runner and your traces are easiest for realistic numbers. We'll share the docker link if you want to run local sims.
[32:59] Tom Hale: Sounds good.
[33:02] Priya Sharma: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items and target the provisioning timeline if we get sign-off.
[33:09] Dana Ortiz: Thanks all.
[33:12] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 2/Marco), some technical terms mistranscribed ("K V cash" instead of KV cache), and timestamps are approximate.

Explicit next steps (restate):
- Priya: price sheet and PO template (send by 2027-10-06)
- Marco: perf sim and recommended batching/quant profile using provided traces (deliver by 2027-10-11)
- Lina: SOC2/ISO + KMS/HSM docs + onboarding checklist (send by 2027-10-06)
- Peregrine (Rajesh): upload 3 workload traces (by 2027-10-07)

End of transcript.
